note: v1 92.46 (seeds 0/11 92.46/92.33), first draft of EUPHORIC ANTHEM, 'Ring Road Sunrise': piano-led liquid D&B, the night's last tune as the sky goes pale. A concert grand plays house-piano stabs on Dmaj9 - E6 - C#m7 - F#m9 in the drops and holds each chord, rolled, outside them; a soaring wordless voice line into a long hall, strings doubling it in the second drop; a straight amen roll with a crash on every phrase, a sub and a low reese pumped by it. The break ends on wM's endless Shepard rise under a snare roll - a climb that never seems to arrive until the last drop lands. Levels on the album standard from the first render: -12.6 LUFS, true peak -1.2 dBTP, longest pinned run 1 (soft-clip-ended master, song volume 0 dB). 2:59.

v2 96.19 (seeds 0/11 96.19/96.16 vs v1 rebaselined 95.54/95.47): THE LIFT and THE CHEST. An anthem needs its key change: the last sixteen bars of the second drop and the outro now go up a semitone, A major to Bb major - piano, strings, the soaring voice, sub and reese all together - so the final run lifts once more just when it should be ending. And it gets a chest: a machine-kit kick under the amen's own kicks (the one and the and-of-3), and the piano's drop stabs gain the left hand's octave on the root, filling the thin low-mids under the roll (spectrum 78 -> 83). Levels stay on the standard: -12.8 LUFS, true peak -1.36 dBTP, run 1; true_peak on.

v3 96.12 (seeds 0/11 96.12/96.09, level with v2 96.19/96.16): THE LIFT WITHDRAWN. v2's last-drop key change (A to Bb) turns out to be the signature of chirper-zero's closer, Streetlights Off - a euphoric piano-and-strings liquid with a wordless hook whose last drop rises a semitone - which I hadn't read before adding it. Taken back out; the chest stays (the machine-kit kick under the amen and the piano's left-hand octave). Ring Road Sunrise and Streetlights Off are too close in kind as well, so the next round moves t3 toward an open lane on the board (reese-led, dark to light) rather than a second piano anthem.

v4 98.63 (seeds 0/11 98.63/98.65 vs v3 96.12/96.09): RE-STYLED, DARK TO LIGHT - so it no longer crowds chirper-zero's euphoric piano closer. The verses are now dark, G minor, carried by a REESE LEAD: a brooding, gliding line in the mid-range whose low-pass breathes on an eight-bar LFO, over a sub, a low pad and the roll - no piano, no voice. In each drop the key turns to its relative major and a concert grand arrives for the FIRST time with house stabs on Ebmaj9 - Bbmaj7 - Fadd9 - Gm9 while the reese steps down to be the bass: the piano is the sunrise, the reese is the road. The break plays the dark line over the light chords. And the handover chirper-zero asked for: the last four bars hold Ebmaj9 over a low G into Hairline's Gm9 (the last 3 s were -52 dB, now -34), with a short tail. Levels: -13.2 LUFS, true peak -1.9 dBTP, run 1.

v5 98.63 (seeds 0/11 98.63/98.65, level with v4): THE DAWN BREAKS - the album's glitch, used once per drop and only at the reveal. The last beat before each drop (the dark reese verse into the light piano) is now caught in a buffer and replayed rising - wM's stutter with a pitch ramp, sixteenth slices climbing three semitones a repeat - so the dark winds itself up into the light and the drop lands on a clean one. A single beat, twice in the track; measured louder than the passage it replaces (the difference sits 3 dB above that beat's level), so it is heard, not hinted.

v6 98.00 (seeds 0/11 98.00/98.02 vs v5 re-scored 98.54/98.55): Ring Road Sunrise's FINAL ROUND, on Harry's notes. The swing and the stutter now agree: the bar whose last beat winds up into the second drop (the rising buffer repeat) plays straight, so the repeats don't fight a shuffled bar. The bass has weight: the sub gains phantom harmonics above 90 Hz and a little drive and pumps harder against the roll, so the dark verses' low end reads on small speakers and the reese lead sits on a floor (the track is 1 dB louder at the same true peak: -12.2 LUFS, -2.0 dBTP). Darker: the top eased 1.5 dB and a 12 kHz low-pass - more night before the sunrise. Kept half a point below the stored best on purpose (the heavier sub reads as low-mid excess to the spectrum term); without the bass change it was 98.39.
